input.rationale: The run's two biggest findings share a mechanism - the blocking send on the FSM mutation channel - so the durable distinction between them is worth stating once, with both sides' evidence, rather than leaving a reader to reconstruct it from separate interpretations: at startup the send is issued before any consumer exists and before NewRaft has returned a handle, which makes it fatal; in the running path the consumer exists and the same select observes the shutdown channel, which a caller can close, and the measured effect of a slow FSM is a per-batch delay rather than a stop.

knowledge.statement: The same blocking send on fsmMutateCh has different consequences at startup and at runtime. In the startup replay the constructor issues it before NewRaft has started the FSM goroutine and before it has returned a handle, so nothing drains the channel and no participant can close the shutdown channel the send also selects on; once the replay needs more batches than the channel holds, the constructor cannot complete. In the running path the FSM goroutine consumes batches and a caller holding the handle can close the shutdown channel, so a slow FSM delays the main loop by about one batch at a time - measured as a backlog that stayed within a single entry behind a 25ms Apply, with and without a buffered apply channel - instead of stopping it.
knowledge.conditions: Startup side: RestoreCommittedLogs enabled with a CommitTrackingLogStore, and a replay window above 128 batches of the configured MaxAppendEntries. Runtime side: the measured configuration is a single-voter in-memory cluster with a 25ms Apply and 400 applies fired without waiting.

knowledge.statement: When RestoreCommittedLogs is enabled and the log store implements CommitTrackingLogStore, NewRaft calls restoreFromCommittedLogs, which sets the commit index from the store and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs delivers the entries in batches of at most config().MaxAppendEntries to the FSM by a blocking select-send on r.fsmMutateCh (created with capacity 128). The only reader of r.fsmMutateCh is runFSM, which NewRaft starts with r.goFunc(r.runFSM) after restoreFromCommittedLogs returns, so during the startup replay nothing consumes the channel.
knowledge.conditions: RestoreCommittedLogs=true, a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore, NewRaft startup path (conf.skipStartup false), entries above r.getLastApplied() present in the log store up to the persisted commit index.

knowledge.statement: For the startup replay, non-return of NewRaft follows from the size of the replay window: with W FSM-bound entries (LogCommand, LogBarrier and LogConfiguration above protocol version 2, per prepareLog) delivered in ceil(W/MaxAppendEntries) batches against a 128-slot fsmMutateCh, the send only fits while ceil(W/MaxAppendEntries) <= 128. Beyond that the startup goroutine blocks in the replay send with no consumer and no way for the caller to reach Shutdown, because NewRaft has not returned a *Raft.
knowledge.conditions: Same conditions as the behavior entry, plus W > 128*MaxAppendEntries; MaxAppendEntries is bounded by ValidateConfig to 1..1024, so the bound is 128*MaxAppendEntries committed-but-unapplied entries (8192 at the 64-entry default).

knowledge.assertion: The replay send happens before any consumer of fsmMutateCh exists.

knowledge.statement: verifyLeader seeds the tally with the leader's own vote (votes=1) and sets quorumSize from quorumSize(), which counts only voters in the latest configuration (voters/2+1); it then registers the verify future in each followerReplication in leaderState.replState, which startStopReplication populates from every server in the latest configuration including nonvoters, and triggers a heartbeat on each. Every successful AppendEntries response calls followerReplication.notifyAll, and verifyFuture.vote increments the tally for every registered future regardless of the responding peer's suffrage, so a nonvoter's acknowledgement contributes to a tally that is compared against a voter quorum.
knowledge.conditions: The node is leader; its latest configuration contains at least one nonvoter whose suffrage is Nonvoter; the nonvoter is reachable while a voter majority is not; VerifyLeader (or the same verifyFuture path) is invoked.

knowledge.statement: A leader that can exchange RPCs only with a nonvoter can obtain a successful VerifyLeader: with three voters and one nonvoter the voter quorum is two, the leader contributes its own vote, and the nonvoter's acknowledgement of an AppendEntries heartbeat supplies the second, so the confirmation is satisfied by an acknowledgement from a server that cannot vote and does not establish that the leader can still reach a voter majority.
knowledge.conditions: Same configuration and partition conditions as the behavior entry; the leader has not yet stepped down through its own lease check, which runs on the LeaderLeaseTimeout timer.

knowledge.statement: The AddVoter configuration change installs the requested server with Suffrage Voter in one step: nextConfiguration's AddVoter branch builds the new Server with Suffrage Voter, the resulting configuration is appended as a single LogConfiguration (or the deprecated remove-peer entry below protocol version 2), and the leader applies it to the commitment and to replication immediately after dispatching it. No captured path creates a Staging server or defers promotion, so the suffrage the operation installs contradicts both published descriptions of the operation (the AddVoter doc comment and membership.md, which lists 'AddVoter: server becomes staging unless voter'), while the promotion loop that membership.md describes is separately declared unimplemented in that same document. The code also deprecates the Staging suffrage and notes that the old AddStaging command was in fact AddVoter, and the Promote command can only act on a Staging server, which no path creates.
knowledge.conditions: Protocol version 2 or above for the ID-based API; the cluster has a leader able to commit the configuration entry; the requested server may be absent from the cluster entirely (a fresh ID and address).

history.statement: The AddVoter configuration change installs the requested server with Suffrage Voter in one step: nextConfiguration's AddVoter branch builds the new Server with Suffrage Voter, the resulting configuration is appended as a single LogConfiguration (or the deprecated remove-peer entry below protocol version 2), and the leader applies it to the commitment and to replication immediately after dispatching it. Nothing in the captured path creates a Staging server or defers promotion, despite the AddVoter comment that describes the server as added for staging and promoted by the leader once it is ready.
history.conditions: Protocol version 2 or above for the ID-based API; the cluster has a leader able to commit the configuration entry; the requested server may be absent from the cluster entirely (a fresh ID and address).
history.correction: The contract source named in the original statement was the AddVoter doc comment alone. The captured membership.md is also a contract source that lists AddVoter as making the server staging, and the same document defers the promotion algorithm, so the statement now distinguishes the suffrage decision (which the code contradicts) from the promotion loop (which the document itself declares unimplemented). The behaviour described is unchanged: the configuration change installs the server as a Voter in one step and nothing creates a Staging server.

knowledge.statement: When the configuration change makes the voter quorum exceed the number of living voters, the cluster loses progress and cannot repair itself in band: the leader's lease check finds contact with fewer voters than the quorum, it steps down, no election can complete because the quorum still requires the unreachable server, applies are answered with ErrNotLeader, and RemoveServer for that server is answered with ErrNotLeader so the configuration still lists it. For one added server this happens exactly when the cluster had a single voter; with two or more living voters, adding a voter leaves the quorum satisfiable and the cluster keeps working.
knowledge.conditions: The added server is not running and no transport can reach it; the pre-change cluster was healthy; captured in-memory timers (heartbeat, election and lease all 50ms in this probe).

knowledge.statement: Uniformly configured clusters keep a cut-off leader's confirmation window ahead of any competing election, and the gate that does it is the peers' refusal to vote while they still have the leader in view: a node with a known leader rejects a vote request from any other candidate before comparing terms, and that knowledge lapses no earlier than its own heartbeat timer, which ValidateConfig keeps at or above the leader's lease. Pre-vote is a second, additional gate rather than the necessary one: with pre-vote enabled an isolated node never raises its term, and with pre-vote disabled it does raise its term and still cannot collect a vote before the lease expires, which is what the pre-vote-disabled run measured.
knowledge.conditions: Nodes sharing their timer settings; ValidateConfig's per-node relation LeaderLeaseTimeout <= HeartbeatTimeout <= ElectionTimeout holding; the candidate isolated from the leader and from a majority of voters. The additional pre-vote gate applies when pre-vote is enabled, which is the captured default.

history.statement: Two gates keep an isolated voter from displacing a leader whose lease is still running when every node shares its timer settings. A node that knows a leader refuses a vote request from any other candidate before it compares terms, so a candidate cannot collect the vote of a peer that still has the leader in view; and with pre-vote enabled the candidate does not raise its term at all while it cannot assemble a majority, because runCandidate's pre-vote phase keeps the node at its current term and only elects for real after the pre-vote is won. Both gates are released by the same event - a peer losing the leader from view when its own heartbeat timer expires - and that timer is reset by the same leader whose lease is expiring, so with shared settings the lease expires no later than the earliest moment at which a vote could be granted.
history.conditions: Pre-vote enabled (the captured default), sending nodes sharing their timer settings, the candidate isolated from the leader and from a majority of voters, and ValidateConfig's per-node relation LeaderLeaseTimeout <= HeartbeatTimeout <= ElectionTimeout holding on every node.
history.correction: The original statement said two gates keep the separation and that the run could not attribute it to either alone. The pre-vote-disabled run shows the higher-term candidacy forming in every trial while the separation still held, so the statement now distinguishes the gate that produces the separation (a peer that still has the leader in view refuses the vote request before comparing terms, and that view lapses no earlier than the peer's own heartbeat timer, which with shared settings is at least the leader's lease) from the additional gate (with pre-vote enabled the candidacy does not form at all). The behaviour described is a correction of attribution, not of the observations.

knowledge.statement: The library's FSM contract asks that Apply be deterministic and that a returned snapshot be cheap to obtain, and it says nothing that bounds how long Apply may block. The leader's delivery of committed entries is a blocking send on fsmMutateCh, so the library transfers the latency of the application's FSM directly into the main loop rather than rejecting or deferring work once the channel is full.
knowledge.conditions: RestoreCommittedLogs is not involved; this is the running path, where processLogs is called from the leader's main loop with futures for the committed entries and runFSM drains fsmMutateCh.

result.summary: One durable statement closes the run, because the two largest findings share a mechanism and a reader should not have to reconstruct their difference from separate interpretations. The fact records that the same blocking send on the FSM mutation channel is fatal at startup and merely delaying at runtime: at startup the constructor issues it before NewRaft has started the FSM goroutine and before it has returned a handle, so nothing drains the channel and no participant can close the shutdown channel the send also selects on — once the replay needs more batches than the channel holds, the constructor cannot complete, which the retained run showed at the boundary of 128 batches with the blocked stack in the replay path. In the running path the consumer exists and a caller holding the handle can close that channel, so a slow FSM delays the main loop by about one batch at a time — measured as a backlog that stayed within a single entry behind a 25ms Apply, with and without a buffered apply channel. It cites both sides' receipts, and it is the statement I would most want a reviewer to take away, since it explains why one blocking send is a defect and the other is backpressure. That is the end of the run's work: three execution-grounded findings with retained receipts, declared comparisons, witnesses and scoped conditions — the startup replay that blocks NewRaft past the channel's batch capacity, the nonvoter acknowledgement that satisfies VerifyLeader's voter quorum and can accompany committed state the confirming leader never applied, and the membership change that installs a voter immediately against two published descriptions that promise staging — plus five suspicions refuted with evidence rather than argument, one behaviour entry corrected under its own id with its affected use answered, fourteen registered questions all answered, and no necessary gap outstanding. Several of my own earlier readings were narrowed or refuted by their own receipts, and those narrowings remain in the record rather than being tidied away.
